newsitem.title: USA: Micron Electronics shrs hit by PC concerns.
newsitem.headline: Micron Electronics shrs hit by PC concerns.

text.p: Shares of Micron Electronics headed down on Wednesday after the company announced its results would likely be hurt by recent price reductions in personal computer systems and higher start-up costs overseas.
Micron shares extended a loss started on Tuesday, falling 1-5/8 to 17 by 0932 EDT/1432 GMT.
On Tuesday, its shares fell 5-3/8 on market worries about the company's upcoming third quarter results -- fears confirmed by the company in a statement after the market close.

Micron Electronics said on Tuesday it expected personal computer sales for the third fiscal quarter would be about 10 percent below sales in the second fiscal quarter, because of recent price reductions and higher start-up costs overseas.

The company said it now expected overall gross margin percentage for the third fiscal quarter ending May 20 to be between two and three percentage points lower than levels experienced in the second quarter.
Start-up costs for international operations, mostly in Japan, would also hurt third quarter earnings, it said.
In March, Micron Electronics reported second quarter gross margins of around 18 percent.

Bear Stearns, which has a neutral rating on the stock, said it lowered its fiscal 1997 earnings estimate on Micron Electronics to $0.90 per share from $1.20 per share and its fiscal 1998 estimate to $1.10 per share from $1.50 per share.
But Bear Stearns maintained the problems Micron Electronics was experiencing were specific to that company and not indicative of industry trends or pressures.

In a research note, analyst Andrew Neff said: "Based on our conversation with Micron Electronics management last night, we believe that this shortfall is as a result of company specific issues...this shortall is not a sign of slower demand or more competitive pricing."
The firm said Micron Electronics faced more compettion from vendors in the direct channel with more resources, like Dell Computer Corp and Gateway 2000 Inc.
Its sales were also closely linked to the highly competitive domestic market and it faced entry barriers in some international markets, Bear Stearns said.
Speculation about Micron's results intensified on Tuesday after the company cancelled a presentation at a Smith Barney Technology conference earlier in the day, traders said then.
